plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1872, 1882 & 1905 (Alexander Schmidt discovers thrombin, Giulio Bizzozero discovers living blood platelets in Turin, and Paul Morawitz maps the four-factor clotting cascade) · 1916 & 1929–1935 (Medical student Jay McLean and William Howell at Johns Hopkins discover the anticoagulant heparin, and Henrik Dam in Copenhagen discovers Vitamin K) · Feb 1933 – Sep 1955 (Karl Paul Link and Harold Campbell in Madison isolate dicoumarol from spoiled sweet clover hay after Ed Carlson's blizzard drive, patent Warfarin in 1948, and see it treat President Eisenhower in September 1955).

teach_overlay.scale: from a medical student whose liver extract refused to clot and chicks bleeding in Copenhagen to a milk can of cow's blood in a Wisconsin blizzard, scientists mastered the life-and-death balance of human blood
